title: Reminiscing John Gokongwei Jr., Humble Billionaire and Generous Philanthropist
keywords: Jack and Jill snacks management trainee
primary_topics: Tribute to the late Dr. John Gokongwei Jr., describing his three major lessons as a taipan and philanthropist, written November 11, 2019 after attending his board meetings as a non-executive director of Robinsons Land Corporation
Three governing principles of Gokongwei's life: (1) Family first and foremost; (2) Value of education; (3) Free competition without rent-seeking or political connections

The Gokongwei business philosophy: transparency via stock market listing, no boss mentality, hiring people smarter than oneself, leading by example, and the 'working from the bottom up' principle applied to children and relatives

Gokongwei's philanthropy: P200M to Ateneo (John Gokongwei School of Management on his 75th birthday), P250M to De La Salle University (Gokongwei College of Engineering on his 85th), and donations to Sacred Heart School, Xavier School, Immaculate Conception Academy
sub_topics: CJP and John's first meeting: late 1960s; bidding for back-to-back Ateneo/Assumption College properties at Padre Faura/M. Adriatico/Pedro Gil; CJP was lawyering for a competitor who withdrew (streets too narrow); Gokongwei happy when told of the withdrawal; became friends; John built Manila Midtown Hotel on the property, later transformed to Robinsons Place Manila

The friendship: John 'never visited or called, much less asked, me any favor, directly or indirectly, during my eleven-year stint in the Supreme Court'; post-retirement, renewed friendship and invitation to sit as RLC independent director

JG Summit Holdings: diversified holdings in food, beverage, airlines, petrochemicals, livestock, farming, financial services, power distribution, power generation and telecommunications; ~US$12 billion combined market cap; also has Chengdu, China real estate

90th birthday dinner (August 11, 2016): 'family-only' at Crowne Plaza Galleria, Ortigas; official family = directors (~500 representatives of 75,000 employees); reminiscences by wife Elizabeth, son Lance, and youngest brother James; daughters (Robina, Liza, Hope, Faith, Marcia) sang familiar tunes with modified lyrics; Lance's baritone performance; grandchildren (led by 21-year-old Jason G. Pe) danced and sang; guests gifted with 'Lessons from Dad' book (authored by Lance with Yvette Fernandez)
Miggy Sandejas anecdote: CJP gave the book to grandson Miggy with the inscription: 'Not being a lawyer, you cannot be a chief justice. But with this book, you can someday be a tycoon!'

Family lesson: orphaned at 13 as eldest, John took care of mother and siblings by buying and selling wares; enduring bond passed to children; Chinese New Year and Autumn Mooncake Festival gatherings; extended family members paid 'what they deserved, no more, no less'

Education lesson: 'voracious reader' -- fiction, biographies, history, tomes, books, three or four newspapers daily, on treadmill, in car, in bathroom, and in bed; enrolled in De La Salle University MBA without a college degree (took additional units, graduated 1977 -- 'one of the proudest moments of his life'); ensured all children finished college (Lance: Wharton summa, double degrees in applied science and finance; James: MIT; daughters: Robina as bodega clerk, Marcia scooping ice cream at Presto)

Competition lesson: businesses not rent-seeking, not dependent on connections -- political, family or otherwise; reliant on free market; transparency via stock listing; no boss mentality; not a power tripper; never asked anyone to do anything he wouldn't do himself; hired people smarter and better; paid them well to stay

Business-family discipline: 'the business is not there to serve the family... We never charge any of our personal expenses to the company. We pay for our tickets on Cebu Pacific, stays at Go Hotels and goods at Robinsons Department Stores' -- family used the family's own brands without preferential treatment

Bottom-up training: Lance as Jack and Jill management trainee with 'an old, used Datsun with a broken aircon'; Robina starting as bodega clerk; Marcia scooping ice cream; 'hindi puede ang puede na' -- excellence was not negotiable

CJP's final weeks with John: 'Until a few weeks ago, he dutifully attended board meetings of RLC and Meralco (where I disclose I am likewise an independent director even before him). Though already wheelchair-bound, he listened patiently... his mind was quite agile and even appreciated my corny jokes during our side conversations.'

stances.claim: Business excellence cannot be separated from personal integrity: John Gokongwei never asked CJP for any favor during his 11-year SC tenure, listed his companies for transparency and accountability, hired the best people and paid them well, and personally paid for his own Cebu Pacific tickets and Go Hotel stays. 'Those who actually have money don't have to flaunt it.'
stances.rhetorical_move: integrity-as-business-practice argument: the same values (transparency, no rent-seeking, no boss mentality) apply to personal conduct as to business operations
stances.confidence: asserted through specific behavioral evidence observed over 45 years

stances.claim: Working from the bottom up -- as management trainee selling Jack and Jill snacks, or as bodega clerk, or as Presto ice cream scooper -- is the non-negotiable training methodology for family members who wish to work in the family business. 'If you don't work, you don't eat' and 'hindi puede ang puede na' (excellence was not negotiable) are the governing rules.
stances.rhetorical_move: bottom-up-as-qualification-standard: working from the lowest rung as the proof of meritocracy even for heirs
stances.confidence: asserted through named examples of Lance, Robina and Marcia

stances.claim: Free competition without rent-seeking -- not relying on political, family, or other connections, but on selling the best quality at the least price -- is the only sustainable model for business growth. Gokongwei's US$12B conglomerate is the proof that rent-free, connection-free entrepreneurship can succeed in the Philippine environment.
stances.rhetorical_move: disproof-of-Philippine-cynicism: the conglomerate as the counter-example to the assumption that Philippine business requires connections to succeed

notable_anecdotes: The first meeting and Robinsons Place origin: CJP was lawyering for John's formidable competitor bidding for the Ateneo/Assumption College property; his client withdrew (streets too narrow); John was delighted. He built the Manila Midtown Hotel, then transformed it into the giant Robinsons Place Manila.

The Miggy inscription: CJP gave grandson Miggy the 'Lessons from Dad' book with the handwritten message: 'Not being a lawyer, you cannot be a chief justice. But with this book, you can someday be a tycoon!'

Lance's management trainee story: after graduating Wharton summa cum laude, Lance worked as a management trainee 'going out and selling Jack and Jill snacks to supermarkets, groceries and sari-sari stores' with 'an old, used Datsun with a broken aircon.'

John's DLSU MBA story: no college degree when he enrolled; had to take additional units; graduated 1977 -- 'one of the proudest moments of his life.' Voracious reader -- fiction, biographies, history, tomes, books, three or four newspapers a day, 'on his treadmill, in the car, in the bathroom, and all the way to bed.'

The final board meetings: 'Until a few weeks ago, he dutifully attended board meetings of RLC and Meralco... Though already wheelchair-bound, he listened patiently to and participated in the discussions; his mind was quite agile and even appreciated my corny jokes during our side conversations.'

one_paragraph_summary: Published November 11, 2019 as a tribute to the recently deceased Dr. John Gokongwei Jr., this piece by CJP -- who first met John in the late 1960s when his client withdrew from a property bid, making John very happy, and who later served as a non-executive director of Robinsons Land Corporation -- frames Gokongwei's life around three lessons drawn from Lance Gokongwei's book 'Lessons from Dad' (co-authored with Yvette Fernandez, gifted to all guests at John's 90th birthday dinner at Crowne Plaza Galleria in 2016). First, family first: orphaned at 13, John took care of his mother and siblings by buying and selling wares; he loved to travel with wife Elizabeth and children to see sights, watch shows and visit museums; he paid extended family members 'what they deserved, no more, no less'; 'the best lessons I learned... were from being with them, observing them, and listening to them at the dinner table.' Second, education: a voracious reader (three or four newspapers daily, reading in car, bathroom and bed); he enrolled in De La Salle University MBA without a college degree, graduated 1977 ('one of the proudest moments of his life'); donated P200M to Ateneo on his 75th birthday (John Gokongwei School of Management) and P250M to De La Salle on his 85th (Gokongwei College of Engineering), and donated to Sacred Heart School, Xavier School and Immaculate Conception Academy. Third, free competition: businesses never rent-seeking, never dependent on political or family connections; transparency via stock market listing; hired people smarter than themselves and paid them well; 'The business is not there to serve the family'; Lance sold Jack and Jill snacks as management trainee in an old Datsun with a broken aircon; Robina started as a bodega clerk; Marcia scooped ice cream -- 'hindi puede ang puede na.' CJP notes that John 'never visited or called, much less asked, me any favor, directly or indirectly, during my eleven-year stint in the Supreme Court,' and closes with the image of a wheelchair-bound but mentally agile John attending board meetings until just weeks before his death, 'even appreciated my corny jokes during our side conversations.'
